understandability.claim: README documents the Minecraft/NeoForge target, build and installation paths, server behavior, configuration, client scanner, privacy and enforcement limits, data-pack extension points, administrator commands, persistence, evidence logs, and security limitations.

verification.claim: The stable candidate records one exact-head gate spanning Build, GameTest, Packaged Server, External Runtime, and Ubuntu/Windows/macOS scanner checks; all required workflows succeeded and all 24 required GameTests passed.

A packaged NeoForge server and real Minecraft protocol client exercised a real block-break packet through BlockEvent.BreakEvent, production warning progression, JSONL evidence logging, and actual connection termination with action=kick.

reproducibility.claim: The build records Java 21, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.235, mod version 1.1.0, test dependencies, production/gameTest source separation, and the Gradle build path.

An isolated offline clean build succeeded and produced a JAR byte-for-byte identical to the GitHub-built stable candidate with SHA-256 4cc843c0c39348203e3ffe30ab4dbd6c33a9eb0f6d2907913d005b89a80588fe.

interoperability.claim: The repository defines exact Minecraft/NeoForge compatibility, separate server-only and optional client installation modes, behavior with FakePlayers and tools from other mods, and data-pack tags that other content can extend.

Scanner and recursive filesystem-watcher behavior passed on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS; this evidence is bounded to scanner/watcher behavior and does not claim a complete graphical Minecraft runtime on all three platforms.

security-safety.claim: The client scanner explicitly documents fail-open/fail-closed policy, high-confidence blocking boundaries, privacy behavior, non-attestation, false-positive limits, and that it is not a tamper-proof or server-enforced anti-cheat.

stewardship.claim: Repository build metadata records MIT licensing and stable version 1.1.0.
The release receipt freezes exact artifact identity and requires publication from the reviewed stable-candidate JAR without rebuilding it after approval.
